scenarios.title: Draft-to-grid and axis selection with cell text menus
steps: Open Draft grid and literal paste in Live Preview. Record complete source. Edit Alpha without changing it; drag text within that cell, then make a held primary-mouse drag into Delta. Inspect one rectangular grid range, no remaining textarea or text selection, and use real Copy then paste into a new scratch note to inspect all selected cell values.

Repeat from another cell while Alpha has a valid changed draft. Keep holding through the remount, move back across Alpha and release. Verify exactly one content commit, no trailing-click edit, accurate grid Copy/Cut/Paste/Delete and one Undo/Redo. Restore the full baseline. Test Escape and pointer cancellation during a held range: selection restores while any committed draft remains separately undoable.

Edit Alpha, right-click Beta, then right-click Alpha without manually closing the menu; also repeat with B in another table of the same note/editor: exactly one menu remains visible and both later menus operate on grid cells. Right-click inside a multi-cell range retains the whole range; outside it selects one cell. Repeat a merged owner and RTL representative. Invalid math and active IME retain the complete draft and refuse crossing or foreign-cell menus.

Open the active editor menu. Exercise text selection, Copy/Cut/Paste, Select all, draft Undo/Redo, bold/italic, line break, finish/cancel and Table operations submenu. Opening/dismissing the text menu or its submenu does not write; a chosen table command commits the draft and command atomically with one Undo. Replacing a menu invalidates old actions and pending clipboard results. Test a refused command and source/file change before action; no partial write. Check fresh unchanged B can Undo committed A using the menu, as with the keyboard. Dismissing menus retains an outside input's focus.

While editing Delta, complete selection of its own row/column and another row/column by click, keyboard, focus and Shift selection. Each successful selection highlights every selected visible owner, closes the textarea and focuses the live grid/handle. Unchanged drafts make no write; valid changed drafts commit once with exact Undo/Redo. Invalid math, IME and stale drafts retain their complete text and prior selection. Use real Copy/Cut/Paste and Delete from the focused handle to check the full selected axis; textarea clipboard remains native, and stale owned selections must not write clipboard or source.

Right-click an axis handle with a changed draft, including in a Callout: the draft commits before the axis menu opens, clipboard sees the committed values, and a later table command has its own Undo step. Invalid/IME/stale drafts refuse both axis selection and menu. A delayed Callout menu must not appear after a newer interaction, menu or source/file change. Hold and drag a handle with a changed draft: draft plus reorder is one write/Undo, with no trailing-click editor. Cancel a pending press or drag with Escape, pointer cancellation, blur or release away from the handle: preserve the draft and restore the prior range/anchors without a write.
expected: A visible grid range owns focus and commands after one safe transition; invalid/composing/stale drafts remain protected.
Menus preserve the intended text/range/file target and use the same draft/history/clipboard rules as keyboard input. Only actually observed input and theme variants count as passed.

scenarios.title: External literal HTML and single-cell plain-text paste
steps:
Open Draft grid and literal paste. On desktop open Literal clipboard.html in an actual browser, use its visible Copy table and Copy single cell buttons, then paste through the real Obsidian note and active-cell entries. Inspect literal Wiki brackets, backticks, comment-looking text, entities, literal
, real breaks and Unicode spaces after commit, reopen and Undo/Redo. Keep actual rich clipboard evidence separate from text-only setup.

Use Paste as plain text in an active cell and single-owner grid menu. Paste the sample with pipe, backslash, tabs, newlines, < and ^ markers, literal Markdown and HTML. Check visible text, exact row/column/merge/header roles and KEEP neighbors. Repeated plain-text paste beside already encoded text remains usable. One merged owner is eligible; multiple owners disable this command.

Test fragment paste beside ordinary punctuation and in code/math/link/HTML source. Unsupported contexts and clipboard denial retain the draft and original table. Change source, file or selection during a pending menu read and verify refusal. Internal Structural Tables range paste retains raw Markdown and topology.

On Android use actual touch and the single-cell menu for plain-text paste, commit and native Undo/Redo. Preserve scrolling, native text selection and existing touch range entry; do not claim desktop mouse or browser-rich cases as mobile coverage.
expected:
External HTML text is displayed literally without creating links, code, hidden comments or a second entity interpretation. Actual breaks remain distinct from literal
.
Plain text changes one visible owner only, preserves table geometry and other content, and cannot bypass stale/clipboard/context validation.

scenarios.title: Native-aligned handle appearance, selection and first-gesture dragging
steps: Open Theme corners and export in Live Preview with ordinary-table takeover disabled and Follow theme selected. Compare its native ordinary table with the structural tables in the same note, host and theme. Record the original note bytes and the exact host/theme identities.

On desktop, hover a structural cell and then each revealed row/column handle. Inspect quiet, hover, selected and keyboard-focus states in Default light and dark mode, adding a pinned third-party theme when available. The fixed-size grip is decorative, only its compact inner background is painted, and the transparent outer button retains its target. No unwanted native button border, shadow or size override may remain. Do not infer current native icon dimensions from old media.

Click a row handle and a column handle, then use Tab and arrow keys to navigate their groups. Selection remains distinct from hover and focus stays visible; the icon adds no focus stop or accessible name. Clear selection by leaving the table and check ordinary native handles remain unchanged.

In Interaction batches, make the first pointer gesture a text selection inside a cell. It must not activate a nearby handle. Press and drag an unselected row handle in one gesture, inspect the exact move, then Undo and Redo once; restore the full-note baseline. Repeat with a column handle and check values, alignment, merged owners and unrelated prose.

Attempt a move that splits a merged owner or crosses header/data roles. It must show the existing blocked feedback without a source write. Check Escape cancellation, a horizontally scrolled table and the Callout table; use Language and RTL for the corresponding physical-direction and keyboard checks.

On Android, use actual touch to inspect the larger row/column targets, select axes, extend a range and drag an eligible selection, then use on-screen Undo. Inspect selected/drag feedback and ensure the compact grip has not reduced the touch target or covered preceding text. Keep mobile observations separate from desktop and browser checks; record unavailable or unobserved combinations as not-run.
expected: Owned handles use native table-handle theme colors and fixed decorative grip icons, with distinct reveal, hover, selection and focus states. Native ordinary tables, table alignment and source text remain unchanged by presentation.

Existing pointer/touch targets, one Tab stop per group, first-gesture text selection and same-gesture axis dragging remain intact. Valid moves form one reversible operation; blocked or cancelled moves preserve the complete note.
The result covers only the actual candidate, host, theme, mode and input combinations observed; omitted native or mobile checks are not reported as passed.

scenarios.title: GFM orientation preview, exact targets and safe replacement
steps: Open GFM preview safety. From the command palette and owned-table menu open the row-header-only table: Swap rows and columns is recommended and Name/Age/City become actual GFM column headers. Compare Keep rows and columns, rendered result and source. Copy each result and compare Markdown content, allowing platform clipboard line endings. Cancel leaves the note unchanged.

Keep the source cursor in the first identical table and invoke conversion from the second table native menu with ordinary-table takeover off, then from its owned menu with takeover on. Confirm one replacement of only the clicked table; one undo/redo restores/reapplies the exact complete note.

Inspect merged cells, multiple header layers and alignment warnings in Structural table; check KEEP HIDDEN disables replacement and warns before copy. Convert the list-contained row-header table and preserve its prefix and surrounding text.

In Reading View use the plugin-rendered table menu: preview and copy are available, replacement is absent. Change the saved table while preview is open and require stale refusal. Also open a replacement preview then change file/source or retain a cell draft: confirmation must refuse.

Check Convert to plain GFM table is grouped with whole-table transpose, while Word / HTML copy and image export remain output actions. Copy the complete table from owned, source, native and plugin-rendered Reading menus. Desktop rich HTML preserves the complete table; Android uses the documented tab-separated fallback notice. Copy writes no Markdown and refuses a source/file change or owner unload during rendering.

Check narrow layout, keyboard focus, Arabic interface with an LTR note, clipboard denial and plugin unload. On Android operate actual touch menus, the soft keyboard and on-screen undo/redo. Record unsupported or unobserved checks independently.
expected: Rendered/source/copy/replacement reflect the selected orientation. Loss of structure is explained; hidden source cells prevent replacement.
Cancel and refused stale/draft paths write nothing. Successful replacement preserves unrelated tables and prose, restores focus, and forms one independent history step. Reading mode is copy-only.

scenarios.title: Native table boundary, right-click target and visual-line navigation
steps: In GFM preview safety use the native ordinary table menu in Boundary to insert a column or change headers; KEEP BEFORE and KEEP AFTER remain exact unrelated prose, then undo. Edit nearby HTML/paragraph boundaries and compare table ownership after view switch/full reparse.

On desktop leave an old source caret elsewhere, then right-click a rendered cell. The viewport must not jump to the old caret or open a different target menu. Inputs, links and buttons retain native context behavior.

Use a narrow cell with long wrapped text, hard breaks and a fractional CSS width. Up/Down leaves only the actual first/last visual line; interior visual lines, selection and uncertain bidi remain native. Verify normal edits and undo/redo.

On Android repeat the affected shared editor/navigation and menu paths with actual touch and soft-keyboard input. Right mouse-button behavior is desktop-only; do not infer mobile input from Chromium or mouse tests.
expected: Native operations cannot absorb adjacent pipe prose; parser-cache ownership agrees with a complete reparse.
Context-menu targets stay under the actual gesture and visual navigation preserves native guards. Full-note source and history remain bounded.

scenarios.title: Native HTML boundaries and exact code clipboard text
steps: Open HTML boundaries and code interchange in Reading View and Live Preview. Compare saved source hashes across view changes. In Reading View verify literal-heading, literal-list and literal-reference retain their attributes and complete pipe text. In Live Preview verify these remain unowned, preserving native HTML or source rendering. The continuation, Callout, escaped-tag and Code export tables render as owned tables. The Callout remains after raw HTML to exercise native-lexer failure recovery: double-click its fallback title to edit the complete quote source, then leave it to restore presentation. The fenced example remains code or native source.

Edit Alpha in the continuation table, commit, undo and redo. Repeat with Beta in the Callout. Compare the complete note before and after each history action; retain surrounding HTML, list indentation, quote prefixes and other tables.

Use the product Copy plain GFM command on Code export. Paste at a blank block boundary in a separate disposable note and inspect the saved Markdown plus the actual rendered code text and every KEEP cell. Preview Convert to plain GFM, cancel without a source change, then confirm and undo once to restore the complete original note. Code spans containing pipes use inline HTML code elements and entities for GitHub GFM and native Obsidian compatibility.

Copy an actual browser HTML table containing code text a|b, a\|b, a\\|b and a\\\|b into Clipboard destination. Verify all text and trailing KEEP cells, then undo and redo the paste. Also exercise plain literal backslashes, a Wiki link, line breaks and merged cells, and verify math/linked/unsupported HTML retains the existing native fallback. Record the external source application and clipboard formats.
expected: Both views respect native HTML ownership, retain valid editable tables and do not mutate Markdown during rendering.
Cell edits, GFM conversion and HTML paste write only the intended table or destination; one undo restores the complete operation baseline and redo reproduces the exact result.

Rendered code text retains every literal backslash and pipe, all columns and trailing cells. GFM inline HTML fallback is documented as requiring a consumer that permits inline HTML; unsupported HTML is not silently truncated.

scenarios.title: Whole-table transpose confirmation and host history
steps: Open Transpose and history in Live Preview with ordinary-table takeover disabled. Retain the fixture identity as input evidence. Click or tap North in the native ordinary table and allow Obsidian to finish any native table formatting. Immediately before invoking transpose, record the complete note source as the native-operation baseline. Use the on-screen command palette to invoke Transpose whole table (swap rows and columns). This deliberately starts with a native cell editor active; it must not report a stale table.

Inspect the mixed-alignment and Structural Tables syntax warnings. Cancel and compare the complete note source with the native-operation baseline. Open the same command again, confirm, and inspect the transposed first table, its header relationships and all values including 00123 and the Arabic text.

Use one host Undo action to restore the exact native-operation baseline and one host Redo action to restore the same transposed result. Do not depend on hardware shortcuts on Android; use Obsidian on-screen Undo/Redo controls.

Finish any cell edit in the owned merged table. Record a separate complete-note baseline immediately before this operation, including the first table's current redone state. Select a cell or partial range, open its context menu with right-click or Android long press, and choose whole-table transpose. Confirm the alignment warning, then undo and redo once. Undo must restore this owned-operation baseline. Inspect the merged region, all cell values, adjoining paragraphs and the other table.
expected: The native-cell command reaches confirmation and writes nothing before confirmation; Cancel preserves the exact full note source.
Confirm transposes the intended whole table regardless of the transient cell/range selection, swaps header roles and merges, and retains every value. Other tables and surrounding prose are unchanged.
Each transpose is one host undo/redo operation. On desktop keyboard undo/redo works immediately after confirmation; Android proves the on-screen history path without requiring keyboard shortcuts.

scenarios.title: Tall-table exit focus, touch pan and soft-keyboard geometry
steps: Open Final cell focus in Live Preview and record the source. On Android, start a real scroll/pan on a visible cell, then promptly tap that same cell once after the pan; it should select without opening an editor or keyboard. A fresh deliberate double tap must still edit. Finish that unchanged edit before continuing.

Use a narrow pane so the long third-column text wraps and the merged table is taller than the viewport. Scroll to the final cell last-24 and pan the local table horizontally to show that cell. Record its horizontal position separately from the note's vertical position. Open it with a desktop click or Android double tap, keep its text unchanged, and inspect the merged table and current scroll position. On Android verify the soft keyboard is visible, dismiss it with the host Back action, reopen the unchanged editor if needed, and compare the table while the keyboard is shown and hidden.

Tap or click the After the table paragraph. Inspect the caret destination, complete merged table, final rows and local horizontal scrolling. Compare source bytes with the recorded source. On desktop repeat after explicitly canceling the final-cell editor with Escape; Android repeats the unchanged-edit/keyboard-dismiss path without requiring Escape.

Repeat from the final cell, change last-24 to last-24x and tap the After paragraph once as a separate action. Check the exact complete note, one committed cell change, the collapsed paragraph caret and retained local horizontal position. Undo once to restore the complete pre-edit note and redo once to restore the same edited result. Repeat unchanged and changed-cell exits with the real host RTL setting enabled, then restore that setting; record each direction separately.

Repeat unchanged and changed-draft exits toward the Before paragraph above the table, scrolling there while the draft remains open and recording the settled position immediately before the click. On desktop also click exposed editor whitespace above and below the prose as separate cases. Each ordinary single click must place a collapsed caret at its actual target; double-click word selection and drag selection must retain their native ranges. Allow natural layout changes when the committed content is shorter, but reject any temporary empty-table collapse or jump to an unrelated source range.

On Android, select a rectangle with two taps and separately long-press inside it to open its range menu. Verify that its actions still target the complete selected range, then dismiss without writing. Record actual touch/keyboard behavior rather than a synthetic pointer-cancel event.
expected: A canceled pan is not reused as the first tap of an edit gesture. One fresh tap does not unexpectedly open the editor or keyboard, and a valid fresh double tap still edits.

Leaving the unchanged final cell preserves Markdown, merged spans, complete rendering and the local table's horizontal position in LTR and RTL. A separate single tap places a collapsed caret in the paragraph below; deliberate multi-tap and long-press text selections remain native.

Leaving a changed final cell commits exactly that cell once, preserves other tables and prose, and retains local horizontal position. Above/below pointer destinations remain correct while asynchronously rendered cells finish; no temporary blank replacement collapses the viewport. One host undo restores the exact pre-edit note; one redo restores the exact edited result.

Soft-keyboard viewport resizing does not replace the table or lose the final rows, and the viewport remains near the intended target after accounting for that resize. A completed range remains available to its long-press menu.

scenarios.title: Interface language independent of note direction and physical column actions
steps: Open Language and RTL in Live Preview with Obsidian Editor Right-to-left (RTL) disabled. Record its source. Inspect all seven native language names in Structural Tables General settings, select Arabic, inspect the RTL settings/dialog text, then return to the note. The table must remain LTR even though one cell and the plugin UI use Arabic.

With the source still unchanged, enable the real Obsidian Editor Right-to-left (RTL) setting for the disposable Vault. Reopen the note if required by the host. Inspect North/Region in the first source column on the right, mixed Arabic/English text, parentheses, 00123 and Arabic digits; switch the plugin language back to English while retaining the host RTL note direction.

In the RTL table, select the English data-column cell ABC-123 and open its table menu. Insert a column left; verify that the blank column is physically left of that cell and that existing values keep their source order. Undo once. Insert a column right, verify the blank column on the physical right, then undo once.

Disable the host RTL setting and switch the plugin language again. Verify that only the intended inserted-column actions ever changed Markdown, their undo restored the initial source, and language/direction changes did not translate, reorder or rewrite any cell. Record an inaccessible host direction setting as an unverified scope rather than replacing it with DOM manipulation.
expected: Native names list English, 简体中文, 繁體中文, 日本語, Deutsch, Español and العربية. Arabic plugin controls/dialogs use RTL independently of the note; other selected plugin languages use LTR.

The real RTL note places the first source column and row headers on the right. LTR notes containing Arabic stay LTR. UI language, cell content and direction switches preserve source order and the meanings of <, ^ and ||.

Left/right insert actions use physical table sides, preserve existing content and header relationships, and each undo restores the exact initial note. Mixed text and digits remain readable without source mutation.

scenarios.title: Reading tables across native sections and adjoining prose
steps: Open Reading boundaries in Reading View. Verify both multi-row headers render as two header rows and all row-header tables render instead of raw pipe paragraphs.

Verify Before/After prose, formatted links and the following ordinary table remain intact. Switch between Live Preview and Reading View, close and reopen the note, and repeat with the plugin Reading View setting disabled and enabled.
Inspect source mode after the view switches and verify source is unchanged. Open a second pane with the same note and confirm independent rendering.
expected: All five structural tables render with their correct cells, headers and source order; adjoining prose and the ordinary table remain visible.
Turning Reading View off restores native output; turning it on restores the owned tables without duplicate or empty replacements.
Source Markdown is unchanged by rendering, reopening and settings changes.

scenarios.title: Explicit math pipe suggestions and retained unsafe drafts
steps: Open Math input in Live Preview. Enter $|x|$ in the Absolute value cell and try saving with Enter. Verify the complete draft remains, open the cell editor menu, dismiss it, reopen it and explicitly choose the absolute-value suggestion.

Enter $P(A|B)$ in the Conditional value cell and explicitly choose the conditional suggestion. Verify both saved sources and two-column geometry; undo and redo, switch to Reading View and reopen the note.

Enter $|x\|$ and $P(\text{A|B})$ in the respective value cells. Verify saving is refused, complete drafts remain and no rewrite is offered. Cancel explicitly. On desktop also try Tab at the final cell and verify it neither navigates nor adds a row.

Repeat the absolute-value confirmation inside the Callout. Inspect native Norm and Fraction rendering and confirm their source is unchanged. On Android use the soft keyboard and a separate long press inside the active editor.

Inspect the Safe math matrix in Reading View and Live Preview, then enable ordinary-table takeover and verify the ordinary math table. Confirm absolute value, norm, conditional separator, matrix and aligned equations keep their intended rendering and exact source after formatting and reopening. In a math cell insert an actual draft newline and attempt a commit; the full draft must remain with no source write. Cancel explicitly.
expected: Only explicit menu selection writes a suggestion; dismissing the menu preserves the complete draft and original table.
Confirmed values store $\lvert x\rvert$ and $P(A\mid B)$, retain two columns and render after undo/redo, view switching and reload.
Escaped boundaries and text-command pipes have no suggestion and cause no source write, row insertion or draft loss.
Callout confirmation keeps prefixes and focus; existing norm and fraction commands retain their source and intended rendering.
Safe single-line TeX, Wiki aliases and image-size pipes remain distinct scanner cases; actual newlines inside math are rejected without converting them to HTML break tags or discarding drafts.

scenarios.title: Base promotion previews break-related content differences
steps: Open Base promotion content with Bases enabled. Invoke Upgrade current table to Base from the command palette. Inspect every content/detail entry, final Property mapping, generated record path and frontmatter preview; verify the acceptance checkbox starts clear and confirmation is unavailable.
Cancel or close the preview. Verify the table source is unchanged and no _structural-table-records directory for this attempt was created.

Open the preview again, inspect the visual-break, code-literal, escaped/entity-literal, math and HTML-uncertain classifications, explicitly accept the listed differences, then confirm the upgrade. Inspect the generated record files and Base values, close and reopen the note and records.

Use the host Undo and Redo controls to reverse and reapply the source-table replacement while verifying generated records remain. With the Base present again, run Restore table from current Base and confirm the original table spellings return while generated records remain.
expected: The preview shows source row/column and source text, distinguishes confirmed and uncertain contexts, reports source-cell and generated-target counts, and exposes the exact prepared record files without executing preview text as HTML.
Cancellation or closing before confirmation performs zero writes; reopening resets acceptance.

Confirmation writes exactly the previewed Property strings and record frontmatter, including
,
,
, case variants and literal/uncertain source spellings; this scenario does not require native Base to render them as multiline rich text.

Undo/redo affects the source replacement without deleting generated files, and explicit restoration recovers the original table from the manifest while keeping generated records. Android uses on-screen command/menu and host undo/redo controls rather than desktop keyboard shortcuts.

scenarios.title: Base promotion failure preserves generated and concurrent content
steps: Open Promotion recovery in a fresh disposable Vault with Bases enabled. Run the acceptance provider command Arm promotion failure, then preview and confirm Upgrade to Base for the Alice/Bob table.
Inspect the failure message, source note and generated directory. Open Alice and check the appended external edit; verify Bob and the recovery manifest remain present.
Upgrade the Carol/Dan table normally, inspect its Base records, and restore the original table while retaining its generated records.
expected: The failed upgrade reports the generated directory path and original stale-table error; no generated directory is trashed.
The first table retains External source change, Alice retains External record edit retained., and the other generated files remain available for manual review.
The normal upgrade shows Carol and Dan in the Base; restoration recovers only its original table and keeps all records from both attempts.

scenarios.title: Interrupted drafts and wide-table editing
steps: Open Reliability checks in Live Preview. Run the provider command Arm conflict on next cell input, edit Alpha and enter draft text; wait for the separate source change.

Confirm the recovery dialog preserves the entered text and identifies the source. Dismiss and reopen it with Recover interrupted cell drafts; copy or select the preserved text, then explicitly discard it.
Edit a cell normally, commit and reopen to verify persistence. Enter a longer draft and cancel it; verify bounded height and stable column width.

In the wide table, select and drag a data-row handle; check blocked-header feedback and cancel a blocked drop. Scroll horizontally and inspect visible controls. On desktop use Tab and arrow keys to reach another column handle.
expected: The source change is retained and the interrupted draft remains accessible after widget replacement and dialog dismissal, without overwriting either cell.
Explicit discard clears the recovery buffer; normal commit and cancel produce no recovery draft.
Normal editing persists and long drafts stay within the table width; canceled or blocked moves leave source unchanged.
The wide table scrolls locally and retains usable controls; desktop keyboard navigation retains a visible Tab entry.

scenarios.title: Edge insertion, terminal Tab and explicit axis dragging
steps: Open Table controls in Live Preview. Use bottom/right add buttons, including with an active cell draft; commit, undo and redo
On desktop, Tab from the final visible cell adds one data row and opens its first cell; Shift+Tab at the first cell creates nothing
Use the bottom button on the header-only table; inspect header roles and the new data row

Press and drag an unselected row handle immediately to a new data-row position; repeat for a column, including with a changed active draft, and verify draft plus reorder is one Undo/Redo operation with no trailing-click editor

With unchanged and changed cell drafts, complete row/column selection by click or keyboard on desktop and handle tap on Android. Inspect complete axis highlighting, no active textarea, live grid/handle focus and subsequent Copy/Clear. Select a range with Shift-click on desktop or two handle taps on Android, preserving the original anchor across any draft commit, then drag a selected handle to move the range
Verify one-gesture drag, partial merged rows/columns, a destination inside a merged group and crossing header boundaries; cancel a valid drag with Escape on desktop or by releasing outside
Repeat insertion and row reorder inside the Callout and deep list; inspect saved prefixes and Reading View
Inspect controls and drop markers in left, centered and full-width layouts, narrow/wide tables, and light/dark theme; verify no page overflow or clipped touch targets
expected: Insertion and any active draft write atomically, retain content and prefixes, and focus the new cell; header-only tables gain data rows

A first held drag moves the newly selected axis; a click completes selection after safely ending the draft, while a selected-handle drag performs one validated reorder on drop and retains the moved axis selection
Content, complete merged rectangles and column alignment move together; invalid and cancelled drops leave source unchanged
Controls remain reachable and align with the table, local horizontal scrolling stays usable, and Reading View has no editing controls
Hardware Tab and Escape claims apply to desktop; Android uses the declared touch driver

scenarios.title: Callout source mapping and asynchronous cell focus
steps: Open Callout mapping in Reading View and Live Preview; inspect every positive case and both protected/invalid examples
Edit the second identical table, commit, undo and redo; inspect the unchanged first table and exact quote prefixes
Edit rich row-header content; traverse cells, fold and reopen a Callout, and switch views
Use the merged-header context menu to split and undo; verify focus and rendered ownership after each operation
expected: All nine valid structural tables render; the ordinary neighbour remains native unless takeover is enabled
Rich row headers, multiple header rows, nested and list Callouts retain their structure in both views
Only the selected table is written; commit and undo/redo restore the rendered cell without exposing whole-Callout source
Fenced examples and invalid row-header syntax stay uneditable; view changes and folding preserve saved source

scenarios.title: Container rendering and safe source writes
steps: Open Container checks in Reading View and Live Preview; inspect callout, nested quote, list and deep list tables
Edit Alpha in the callout table and One in the list table; commit, undo and redo
Format a container table with preview and confirmation; split and merge its header
Inspect source after writes and verify every container prefix, YAML scalar and fenced example
Edit the plain paragraph before the tables, then edit a table cell to verify the shifted source binding
expected: All four tables render with merged headers in both views
Editing and formatting retain quote markers and list indentation; undo and redo restore exact content
YAML and fenced examples remain untouched and are never acquired as editable tables
Safe prose edits leave table rendering and subsequent cell edits correctly bound

scenarios.title: Structural rendering and invalid source
steps: Open the valid table in Reading View and Live Preview
Open Complex headers in Three-line style in both views; inspect nested column groups, combined row/column spans, and the simple reference
In Reading View, compare the later native alignment and empty-geometry references with their own Markdown source
Compare the owned content-left table origin with the native ordinary-table reference

Render cells containing
,
, and
in Reading View and Live Preview, then preview formatting
Open the invalid table and inspect its diagnostic
Render a row-header table containing emphasis and Markdown links beside an ordinary table
expected: Column spans, row spans, multi-row headers, and row-header boundaries render consistently
Three-line group rules appear only under spanning titles with child headers, remain inset at each end, never cross row-spanning headers, and add no rules to the body or simple header
Each later ordinary table renders its own rows and columns instead of repeating an earlier structural table
Overlaid row and column handles do not shift the owned table's content-left alignment away from the native reference
All three break-tag spellings produce a visual line break and formatting preserves the exact source spelling
Rich inline formatting preserves row-header rendering and never causes a later ordinary table to be replaced
Invalid syntax retains its source and reports a bounded diagnostic

scenarios.title: Cell editing, selection, focus and navigation
steps: Open the in-place editor with a desktop single click or Android double-tap
On Android, select a rectangle with two taps, then separately long-press a selected cell and merge; split it, start a new range outside the selection, and double-tap a selected cell to edit
Compare the table and column geometry before and during cell editing, and inspect the editor border and resize affordance
Hover cells in content-left and content-center layouts and inspect the corresponding row and column handles
Select an owned cell, move focus or the editor cursor outside it, then select a cell in the other owned table
Open Editing checks; edit the introduction before a rendered table, then edit a cell; also keep a cell draft open while an unrelated source change shifts the table
Navigate forward and backward through vertically and horizontally merged cells with Tab and Shift+Tab

Inspect owned Live Preview cell, row and column menus: selected-cell clipboard, available structure/header actions, rows, columns, alignment, adjacent whole-table Word/HTML and PNG outputs, source/Base, clear content and final whole-table deletion. Compare uniform and mixed column alignment and current/different header counts. On desktop activate an action after menu focus transfer, then retry an old action after changing source

Enable ordinary-table takeover and inspect the same menu organization; disable takeover and verify Obsidian's native items remain with applicable plugin contributions. In Reading View verify the brief whole-table PNG entry
expected: Desktop single-click editing works while Android retains double-tap editing and touch selection
A subsequent long press preserves the completed touch rectangle and its range menu; tapping outside starts a new range and double-tapping still edits a cell
Editing does not widen the table or its column and shows one outer focus border without an inner textarea border or resize grip

Only the hovered cell's row and column handles reveal, remain reachable without clipping, and align to the actual table rectangle; always-visible touch column handles reserve space without covering preceding text
The previous cell and handles lose selected styling when focus or the editor cursor leaves, and selection never remains on two owned tables
Unchanged tables retain current source bindings and open drafts after source shifts, including when preceding tables change their indexes
Tab and Shift+Tab visit each visible anchor once without loops or skipped cells

Owned menus group actions by scope in the declared order; row/column deletion stays last in its respective group and whole-table deletion has a separate final warning group. Uniform selected-column alignment has one check, mixed alignment has none; identical header counts are omitted while eligible content-preserving removal remains available

Menu activation retains the frozen logical selection through focus transfer and revalidates source before acting; real source changes refuse the stale action. Ordinary native menus and Reading View's brief PNG entry remain available without adopting the owned editing menu

scenarios.title: Theme, empty cells and bounded table geometry
steps: Open Empty geometry and compare cell and editor dimensions before, during, and after editing, merging, and splitting, first with fresh theme density and then comfortable and compact densities
Open Width and format checks and inspect long unbroken content before and during editing in narrow and split panes

On desktop, compare default and pinned Minimal theme table widths in light and dark mode with note-level table-wide, table-max and table-100 classes; switch Theme/Grid/Three-line styles and all density/layout options, including merged cells and multi-row headers. Keep third-party exporters disabled for this baseline and record each exercised combination separately. Rounded-corner checks belong to theme-corner-export.
expected: Empty cells retain at least one line of content height in every density; cell and table geometry remains stable when entering or cancelling editing and usable through merge and split
Editing does not widen the table or its column and shows one outer focus border without an inner textarea border or resize grip
Owned blocks stay inside the text column under theme width classes; wide content scrolls locally and does not widen the page

scenarios.title: Multiline clipboard and source formatting
steps: Insert a break with Shift+Enter and the cell-editor context menu, then paste multiline text and a browser or Excel cell containing a line break
Preview the format command before confirming a canonical rewrite
Confirm the rewrite aligns source pipes around ASCII, CJK, row-header dividers, alignment markers, escaped Wiki-link pipes, and code-span pipes without changing the note's line endings
expected:
Editor and imported line breaks become canonical
, and semantic HTML export contains real break elements
No Markdown changes before explicit format confirmation
Every explicit rewrite remains parseable and pipe-aligned by display width while rendering alone never changes Markdown

scenarios.title: Base membership property and explicit legacy migration
steps: Open Legacy Base and confirm its legacy record is visible
Run Migrate legacy Structural Tables Base properties from the command palette
Confirm retired record-ID cleanup starts disabled, review each file's intended actions and zero selected-removal count, enable cleanup, verify the count and actions update, then confirm
Reopen Legacy Record and Legacy Base
expected: The preview names both fixture files and their intended actions before any write, with cleanup initially disabled
Legacy Record contains a structural-tables list and keeps its user property and body
structural_table_ids and structural_record_id are absent after confirmed cleanup
Legacy Base uses bracket access for structural-tables and still shows the record

scenarios.title: Headerless tables and content-preserving header roles
steps: Open Header roles in Live Preview and Reading View. Inspect all seven tables, including Callout and list containers; view changes alone must not change source.
Edit the first data row, add a row and column, then undo and redo. The headerless tables must keep zero column-header rows and every original data row.
On the Name/Value table, select its complete first row and choose Remove column headers. Set the first row as column headers again, then undo and redo. Inspect text and focus.
Try setting only the first column of the horizontally merged Group row as row headers. The boundary through the merge must be refused.
Switch Follow theme, Grid and Three-line in light/dark mode. Inspect row-header alignment, header hierarchy and selected-cell feedback.
expected: Headerless tables render without an empty thead, including the single-row table and both containers; passive rendering preserves source.
Edits and insertion preserve headerless roles, text and alignment; undo/redo restore the table and usable focus.
Removing column headers changes their role while retaining Name and Value as data; restoring headers retains all text. Merge boundaries cannot be split.

Grid semantic headers share a restrained fill and weight. Three-line row headers add no vertical rule or fill; headerless tables have top/bottom rules only. Explicit alignment, selection and Follow theme styling remain correct.

scenarios.title: Ragged GFM rendering and hidden-source write protection
steps: With ordinary-table takeover disabled, inspect Hidden left marker and Hidden above marker in both views. They must retain the native table UI. Enable takeover and repeat refusal and source-preservation checks on both tables.
Enable Take over ordinary Markdown tables and open GFM write safety in Live Preview. Missing cells in Short row must render empty; explicitly edit the first cell and inspect the saved two-column row.

On Hidden left marker, enter a cell draft and attempt commit. Without changing that rejected draft, move to Hidden above marker and open its first cell; repeat with the two tables visible in separate panes when available. During an IME composition on a rejected draft, move focus to another app control before composition ends; completing composition must not pull focus back. Open and dismiss the cell context menu separately and verify its temporary focus handoff returns to the draft. The draft must remain recoverable, focus and menus must stay responsive, and source must remain unchanged. On desktop also attempt terminal Tab.
Attempt merge, row/column insertion, header-role changes, formatting, Convert to GFM, Sheets migration and Upgrade to Base. Inspect source after each operation and confirm no Base files are created.
Copy the visible table as HTML/GFM/CSV/TSV. Switch views and toggle ordinary-table takeover. Recheck the exact original hidden-source row.
expected: Short rows read correctly and safe explicit edits normalize missing cells without losing data.

Every hidden-source write is refused, KEEP and the complete source remain unchanged, failed drafts remain available, switching tables or panes does not create a focus/refocus loop, and Base promotion creates no files.
Copy remains available; view changes and takeover changes do not write source. Terminal Tab is a desktop keyboard check; Android uses touch editing and menus.
Hidden < and ^ cells do not claim structural ownership; enabling takeover keeps them read-only without dropping the extra source cell.

scenarios.title: Base record filenames, bilingual commands and retained restoration
steps: Open Base filename collisions in Live Preview and preview Upgrade to Base. Cancel once and verify no files were created. Reopen and confirm conversion.

Verify the four records retain Alice, ALICE, I and i with values 1, 2, 3 and 4; record paths must be distinct even when compared without case. Move or rename a generated record and verify it remains in the Base.

Switch plugin language between English and Simplified Chinese using the General tab. Check the actual create-record and restore commands against the README. Restore the original table and verify every generated record remains.
expected: Cancel creates no files; confirmation creates four distinct records with all original values.
Moving or renaming a record keeps its Base association. Restoring reproduces the original table and retains all generated records.
Settings retain General, Views and Appearance tabs; bilingual command names match user guidance.

scenarios.title: Source handoff and standalone Markdown rendering
steps: Open Interoperability in Live Preview. Edit North to North edited using the cell editor, commit, then undo and redo. Confirm merged geometry and literal markers remain correct.

Open the rendered North cell menu and choose Edit table source. Open and dismiss an external command panel; return to the raw editor and verify the original caret or range is retained, with no scroll to an unrelated table.

Save the note. Run Preview standalone table rendering from the acceptance provider. Inspect the cloned modal output: North edited spans two rows, Sales and 10 span two columns, literal < and ^ remain visible, and the Callout retains its merged Team/Result table. Close the modal.
Switch between Reading View and Live Preview, then edit the Callout cell 20 to 21 and commit. Undo and redo and verify only that cell changes; the callout and surrounding prose remain intact.
expected: Native source ownership survives external controls without relocating the caret or losing a draft. Explicit source handoff addresses the selected cell.

The standalone clone contains completed text and semantic spans; escaped literals remain literal and render-only operations do not modify the note. Provider preview is standalone-renderer coverage only, not proof of Export Image or saved PNG interoperability.
Cell commits and history preserve the corresponding source, table geometry and Callout prefixes.

scenarios.title: Theme corners and ordinary-table export ownership
steps: Use pinned Maple in light and dark mode with Follow theme and ordinary-table takeover off, then open Theme corners and export in Live Preview and Reading View. Inspect the covered final row, layered headers and Callout in both views: only the four logical outer corners are rounded, including the spanning anchors; internal header corners remain square.

In Maple light mode with ordinary-table takeover disabled and Follow theme selected, export the saved note through pinned Export Image and save the actual PNG. Inspect all text, spans, Callout and explicit left/center/right alignment, including the separate Chinese rows and the br cell. Enable takeover, choose Grid appearance, export again and verify the ordinary table now follows the same owned appearance as the structural tables. In Reading View check Grid and Three-line with takeover on, then disable takeover and verify native ordinary rendering returns while structural tables retain the selected appearance.

With Follow theme restored and takeover off, compare Minimal and the built-in theme in light/dark mode in Reading View and Live Preview. Switch Maple to Minimal to the built-in theme and back to Maple without reopening the note. Square-theme tables must not acquire rounding or retain the previous theme radius; Maple rounding returns. Check Grid and Three-line remain unchanged by theme-corner remapping.

Compare fixture bytes before and after all render/export/settings operations; inspect the saved PNG separately from the preview. Record exact host, theme and exporter identities and retain representative images. Record each theme, mode, view/output, appearance and takeover combination separately using the representative matrix in docs/ACCEPTANCE.md. If a prerequisite exporter or theme is absent or a combination is not exercised, record uncovered checks and a partial or unverified scenario rather than treating provider preview or a subset as complete real export acceptance.
expected: Native theme rounding is retained at logical table corners despite row spans, row headers and layered headers, with no dummy cells added to the actual table.
Export Image preview and saved PNG retain completed content, merged geometry and explicit alignment. Ordinary-table ownership follows the opt-in setting in standalone rendering.
Theme changes do not leave stale rounding; square themes and non-theme appearances retain their intended styling. Source bytes are unchanged.

scenarios.title: Native complete table PNG preview, clipboard and Vault saving
steps: In a fresh host before opening notes with math, export the plain merged table in Editing checks from owned Live Preview and Reading View; restart between the two cold-start checks. Inspect and save each final PNG with unchanged source bytes. Afterwards open Math input, export a math table and inspect completed formula glyphs. Literal link-target dollars, escaped dollars and code must not trigger math work when the host renders them as text.

Open Table image export. Use source command palette, owned Live Preview and Reading menus, then a native ordinary-table menu with takeover disabled. Export the intended table and compare source hashes before and after.

Inspect the reconstructed five-column meal table. Verify noon/evening colspan 2, date rowspan 3, category rowspan 2 and equal left alignment of both right-side dish names. This is a screenshot reconstruction, not the reporter's original source and not proof of an issue fix.

Export Local image and math plus existing Math input fixtures. Inspect the final PNG preview, save to the Vault, independently decode and open that PNG, and paste Copy image into an image-capable application. Check actual rich text, formula glyphs, red/blue SVG attachment pixels and line breaks; original TeX, placeholders or borders alone do not pass.

Export the wide unbroken table and the 30-row table while horizontally scrolled or with controls visible. Inspect the last column, last row, Chinese text, background, spans and explicit alignment in final pixels. Repeat selected Follow theme/Grid/Three-line and Default/Minimal/Maple light/dark combinations.

Cancel a delayed render, repeat export and close/unload the plugin. Change table or theme during generation and verify refusal; completed snapshots stay stable. Try missing or tainted images, unsupported note embeds, denied clipboard/file writes and an oversized table; verify explicit errors and no partial PNG or source write. Recheck existing Word/HTML, GFM/CSV/TSV/range copy and actual third-party Export Image separately.
expected: Preview, copy and saving share the same completed PNG bytes; saving follows public attachment APIs, avoids overwrites and does not insert a Markdown link.
Complete content and supported local resources become actual pixels, without controls, drafts, viewport cropping or silent missing content. Unsupported resources and resource limits fail clearly.

Cancellation and unload release offscreen DOM, subscriptions and object URLs; source Markdown remains unchanged. Native PNG and third-party export observations stay separate, and uncovered host/platform combinations are reported accurately.

scenarios.title: First-click editing, visual arrows, axis gestures and anchored paste
steps: Open Interaction batches in a disposable Vault, record the complete Markdown, and keep at least two tables plus the Callout visible
Edit Alpha and click Beta once with a real full pointer gesture, then immediately type; repeat with unchanged text, cross-table destination and the Callout
With rejected markup or IME composition in Alpha, click another cell; check that the old draft remains recoverable without navigation
Click the rich text samples, double-click to select a word, Alt-click a link label to edit and click normally to activate its link; drag text and Shift-select a grid range separately
Wrap long text in a narrow pane, including a draft tall enough to show its vertical scrollbar; compare Up/Down on outer visual lines versus internal hard/soft lines, RTL and mixed direction
Hold and drag an unselected row/column handle once; repeat with Shift extended and touch-extended ranges and block a partial merge/header crossing

Copy an owned 2x2 range, click one unmerged target cell and paste while its unchanged textarea is open; expand right/down, overwrite in-bound old values, refuse partial merge or changed/composing drafts and validate exact source plus Undo/Redo
Modify A and click B; before changing B, use Ctrl/Cmd+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z/Ctrl+Y to undo/redo A, preserving focus and unrelated tables
Repeat while switching file or source during a clipboard await; a stale paste or Cut must write nothing
expected: One click commits the old valid draft and enters B before the next keystroke, with one exact write and no unrelated source changes; IME/rejected edits keep the old draft
Markup carets map only when unique, ambiguities use a collapsed end caret, ordinary links still activate, and visual/text/grid selections stay separate
Up/Down only exits at proven visual boundaries while retaining horizontal caret position; IME/selection/mixed bidi keep native editing
One gesture reorders the complete selected axis; header, merge, pointercancel and Escape blockers preserve source
Anchored paste expands only as necessary, preserves source syntax and unrelated values, refuses partial merges and unsafe owner topology, and commits once with undo/redo focus

scenarios.title: Clipboard nonbreaking spaces and bounded Sheets migration
steps: Open Clipboard fidelity and migration. Use the acceptance provider sample command to copy edge NBSP, only NBSP, figure spaces and narrow NBSP as setup; paste each into the product cell editor and commit. Leave/reopen the note and record the source and rendered code points. Exercise actual undo/redo and preserve KEEP-CELL, KEEP-ROW and the complete surrounding note.

On desktop copy the browser-rendered Clipboard fidelity.html table and paste into the note through the product. Verify interior and edge spaces, space-only cells, code and Wiki text. Repeat a real single HTML-cell copy into an active cell and commit; do not replace real clipboard input with a synthetic paste event. Android covers native plain-text cell paste and commit; record rich HTML clipboard scope separately.

Invoke Sheets Extended migration on the standalone table, then undo and redo. Invoke migration on the table immediately below KEEP-BEFORE and confirm refusal without a source/history change. Preserve KEEP-AFTER and other tables.

Record clipboard fidelity observations after the relevant actions. On Android use actual touch, native Paste and host Undo/Redo controls; provider setup and observation never substitute for product interaction.
expected: Nonbreaking edge and space-only characters survive actual paste, commit, reopen and rendering; code/Wiki interior text remains unchanged.
Valid migration changes only its table, one undo restores the complete baseline, and the boundary-risk migration writes nothing.

scenarios.title: Unload boundaries for real previews and in-flight operations
steps: Open Operation safety. Record the full-note baseline. In Prepare operation safety boundary choose Unload Structural Tables in 60 seconds, then open the actual Format preview. Observe the preview open before unload, then automatic closure and zero source changes. Inspect both timed-plugin-unload-armed and timed-plugin-unload-completed observations, including before/after visible previews and actual loaded state; a timer that fired before the preview opened does not prove closure. Reload using the provider and open a fresh Format preview; cancel once, reopen and confirm through the product UI. Record old-preview closure and new-instance success separately.

Repeat timed unload with the actual Upgrade current table to Base preview. Reload, arm pause-first-record, then use the actual promotion preview and confirmation. At the Paused fixture I/O modal unload, reload and resume. Inspect the source, first generated record and directory: retain created content, report partial completion, and create no later record or manifest. Record the exact paused stage and file inventory.

On desktop only, reopen the original safety table in a fresh disposable Vault, arm pause-attachment-path first, then open its PNG preview and click the actual Save PNG action. At the I/O gate unload and resume; verify zero new binary files. Reload and use a fresh PNG preview and Save PNG action successfully. Android must record the existing desktop-only PNG limitation rather than claim a PNG save.
expected: Unloading closes retained product previews and starts no later operation from those previews; reloading registers usable new-instance commands. Cancellation and stale confirmations do not change source.
The first-record gate is actually observed, already-created files remain, later files and source replacement do not begin after unload, and the error explains partial completion.

The desktop attachment-path gate actually triggers before the binary write; unloading prevents a saved attachment, while a fresh instance can save an actual PNG. Mobile PNG is explicitly outside the supported surface.

scenarios.title: Original file ownership, dirty panes and conditional migration compensation
steps: In a fresh disposable Vault open Operation safety, choose Prepare migration records, wait for metadata readiness, then arm replace-at-process. Invoke the actual migration command and confirm. Inspect the same-path identical replacement, retained original, error and provider observation. The original TFile must differ from the replacement and neither may receive the stale migration.

Repeat in a fresh Vault with dirty-at-process. Confirm migration through the real preview, then inspect both open panes and the recorded buffers before dismissing or saving anything. The two differing unsaved buffers must remain intact; stale migration must be refused without forcing either buffer to disk. Record any host auto-save as a separate limitation, never infer unsaved preservation from a disk-only check.

Repeat in a fresh Vault with pause-migration. Confirm through the actual product preview, unload and reload at the provider I/O gate, then resume. Verify zero membership writes and an unload error. New-instance commands must still work.

Repeat in a fresh Vault with rollback-external-edit. Confirm through the actual migration preview, observe first completed write and the injected second-write failure, and inspect compensation: original membership and retired ID are restored, the later external body edit remains, and the second target is unchanged.

Finally prepare the two records in a fresh Vault without arming a wrapper. Preview and confirm migration with retired-ID cleanup enabled. Inspect both actual files: membership migrated and IDs removed, while leading/membership/flow comments, quoted scalar, large integer, date, flow mapping layout and body bytes are preserved. Reopen the records and migration command.
expected: Same-path identical replacement is refused based on original TFile ownership, with no stale write to either file.
Conflicting open buffers are detected at the actual process boundary and preserved; the observation records both buffers and the disk state without assigning a verdict.
Unload during delayed migration prevents any new mutation across reload, while the new plugin instance remains usable.
Conditional rollback reverses only the migration-owned changes and retains the external edit after an actual partial-write failure.

Unarmed positive migration succeeds through the product UI and preserves unrelated YAML layout/comments and body bytes. Every injected boundary must have a recorded triggered observation; arming alone is not a pass.

scenarios.title: Whole-table import, Base restoration and copy invocation ownership
steps: Open Whole table boundaries and record its complete source. On desktop copy an actual browser-rendered two-column HTML table from Literal clipboard.html. Select only PLACEHOLDER in the adjacent-body and adjacent-header cases and use the real note-editor Paste. Both must refuse without source, selection or history changes; IMPORTANT THIRD CELL and KEEP text remain visible. A synthetic paste event is not rich clipboard acceptance. On Android record the actual available note-editor clipboard representation and retain unavailable HTML scope as unverified.

Paste into the isolated control. Check the imported table owns only the selected source range and the following three-cell pipe prose remains a separate visible paragraph. Use one host Undo and Redo, compare complete source, then repeat a partial quote/list source-line selection and verify zero-write refusal.

Upgrade the Base restoration table through the actual product preview. Add the marked three-cell prose immediately after its closing fence without a blank line. Invoke Restore original table and confirm the preview: refuse with the Base, prose, records and history intact. Add one blank line, restore successfully and use one host Undo/Redo. Repeat with two-cell prose immediately before the opening fence; record generated record inventory.

In settled Source mode place the caret in A, run the provider's Arm one HTML copy renderer gate, then the real product Copy current table as HTML. Wait for the persistent caught/holding A after the real renderer completed notice. Only this triggered successful-result hold establishes the injected product await boundary; armed-only, a catch before the copy command, renderer failure, Disarm or timeout cannot pass. Invoke a newer real command or menu copy on B, inspect actual clipboard output, then use Release HTML copy renderer gate. B must remain latest with no late A notice. Rearm A separately, wait for caught/holding, disable the tested plugin through host UI while keeping the provider enabled, then Release. A must remain silent; re-enable and copy B successfully. Retain the visible caught signal, action order and diagnostic-only _html-copy-gate-observations.json. No cancellation claim applies to a system write already dispatched; this gate does not measure natural rendering latency.

For a separately armed and visibly caught/holding A command copy, make an ordinary source edit without a newer copy, then Release. The captured A snapshot remains a valid command result; menu targets still reject actual source staleness. Check source bytes remain unchanged by all copy actions, and distinguish desktop rich HTML from mobile TSV fallback. The one-cell renderer wrapper is fixture-only, expires after two untriggered minutes or five captured minutes, and is released by Disarm or provider unload.
expected: Both whole-table write entries preserve unselected prose and hidden source cells, refuse unsafe boundaries with zero writes, and accept isolated controls with full-note Undo/Redo.

Overlapping copy intent and plugin lifetime prevent old post-cancellation dispatch and notices while preserving legitimate command snapshot semantics. Only actually triggered host boundaries count as observed.
